Immersive art became an anchor tenant

The digital art room stopped being a pop up. It is now a permanent institution that developers build cities around.

01 Field notes

teamLab drew millions to a single museum

teamLab Borderless, reopened in Tokyo's Azabudai Hills with more than 75 works, welcomed about 1.69 million visitors in 2025. Across its two Tokyo museums teamLab pulled over 4.2 million people in a year, a footfall most retail anchors would envy.

See the pull ›
02
In the lab

Europe is building its largest immersive room

In Hamburg, the UBS Digital Art Museum opens in spring 2026 as Europe's largest home for digital art: 6,500 square metres, 12 metre ceilings, with a permanent teamLab Borderless as its star. A bank put its name on an immersive museum. That is the tell.
